data.one_liner: A library for encoding and decoding dynamic structured data like JSON and YAML into Dart objects.
data.what_it_does: It converts dynamic and structured data formats like JSON and YAML into typed Dart objects by extending a `Coding` base class. It handles object references, cyclical data, and dynamic type casting for collections like lists and maps.
use_when: You need to serialize and deserialize complex JSON or YAML data structures into custom Dart classes manually.
You are dealing with document references or cyclical data graphs in structured formats.
You prefer runtime serialization logic over code generation tools.
avoid_when: You prefer compile-time code generation for your JSON models.
You want a lightweight, zero-boilerplate serialization solution.
strengths: Supports decoding and encoding of nested custom objects, lists, and maps.
Handles document references ($ref) and cyclical data structures natively.
Provides built-in type coercion and casting support for primitive type arguments.
weaknesses: Requires manual implementation of encode and decode methods for every class.
Minimum Dart SDK requirement is relatively strict (>=3.12.0).

alternatives.name: json_annotation
alternatives.why_pick_it: Provides compile-time JSON serialization using code generation instead of manual runtime decoding methods.

alternatives.name: built_value
alternatives.why_pick_it: Provides immutable value types and builder patterns with robust code generation for serialization.

alternatives.name: freezed_annotation
alternatives.why_pick_it: Generates immutable union and data classes with built-in JSON serialization capabilities.
